_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for NKE retrospectives (retro/build_nke.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern); every NIKE earnings release of the period came after the close, and each call transcript was furnished by its own 8-K a few days later. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), the latest call's outlook words for the current fiscal year published by AS_OF, and events published since that vintage. NIKE's fiscal year ends May 31. Values are as reported, per share on the basis of the filing that published them; a vintage takes each year from the latest 10-K that reports it, and eps_published / shares_published give such a year's own publication date, so a stock split ('splits') restates exactly the per-share facts published before its effective date; a dividend declared on the basis of a split not yet effective carries that basis ('basis', the split's effective date). NIKE gave no revenue or pre-tax margin guide in numbers in any filing of 2007-2017, and no EPS guide in numbers other than the Q1 FY15 call's growth of 'about 20% for the full year' ('eps_growth'): the outlook on its calls is otherwise in words, gross-margin changes at times in basis points ('guides' hold them, display only). A print's margins and growth rates are derived from the published income statement and balance sheet (the raw figures are in its notes); lc_pct is the release's revenue growth less the currency effect it states, or from Q3 FY09 the growth excluding currency changes it states; eps_q is diluted EPS (from continuing operations once the release reports them, from Q2 FY13), excluding non-comparable items where the release publishes that figure (GAAP in the note). From Q2 FY17 the releases no longer state futures orders: a print's 'futures_later' holds them from the first filing that does (the call transcript or the 10-K), with that filing's own date, and before it, as from Q1 FY18 when NIKE stopped reporting them, the print has none (the signal scores BASE). 'events' hold 10-K wording that puts a disruption theme on the watch list (ECOMMERCE from the FY2017 10-K). rule_t holds the ten annual values (FY1998-FY2007) behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.
